description: We are two master’s students at BTU Cottbus. Anantyam means “limitless,” a name inspired by the possibilities NASA opens up for exploration. For Flame in Freefall, we’re using AI to make NASA’s research on fire in microgravity easier to explore. We’re new to combustion science, so we’re learning the subject as we build.
summary: FireLens is an interactive dashboard that makes NASA’s spacecraft fire and smoke research easier to explore. It shows how smoke behaves in a simplified cabin illustration, compares published experiments and detector specifications, and ranks studies by relevance to a spacecraft, Moon base, Mars base, or pressurized rover. FireLens distinguishes measurements, simulations, and planned tests so users can see where evidence is still missing. Each claim links to its original source, with an exact excerpt and location in the Source Inspector.
details:
FireLens addresses Flame in Freefall by summarizing published combustion research, ranking studies for mission conditions, and interpreting the evidence with citations. See it illustrates smoke movement as users change gravity and airflow. Measured and Detectors pair published measurements and equipment specifications. Explore compares experiments by hardware, fuel, atmosphere, and sensors. Habitat relevance explains how each study scores, and Mission briefings show what researchers measured and where more testing is needed. Ask retrieves relevant evidence and Data exports cited values and conditions as CSV or JSON.

The app uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Canvas. It stores source snapshots with SHA-256 hashes and checks excerpts against the stored source text during the build. Search, ranking, and interpretation use fixed rules. We used Grok Bot and OpenAI Codex to help develop and document FireLens.

Source code: https://github.com/rahul-n18/firelens
